assets/style.css.purpose: Whole site's CSS: design tokens, responsive nav, good/bad example blocks, checklist styling, light/dark mode, print stylesheet, logical (RTL-safe) properties. Turncount 10: unified header/main/footer to one shared --content-width (was misaligned at 60rem vs 42rem), added a decoupled --prose-width for flowing text, a --content-width-wide/.wrap-wide shell for the home page's card grid, real depth (shadow tokens, hover lift) on cards, and custom-drawn checklist checkboxes + a details/summary chevron replacing bare default widgets. Turncount 14: added the Craft component block -- course-meta/course-progress badge, lesson-progress-list + lesson-check states, lesson-nav, and the full quiz component (options, hover/disabled/correct/incorrect states, feedback panel) plus matching print rules. The course-progress badge's display rule is deliberately split into `.course-progress:not([hidden]) { display: inline-block; }` plus a separate unscoped properties block -- a plain `.course-progress { display: inline-block; ... }` has the same specificity as the UA stylesheet's `[hidden] { display: none }` and silently wins the tie, defeating the hidden attribute (caught via a real Playwright test, not by reading the CSS). Turncount 21 (QoL audit): dark-theme variables now apply via both the `prefers-color-scheme` media query (system default) AND an explicit `:root[data-theme]` attribute selector (reader's manual override always wins); added `.theme-toggle` button styles with a CSS-only icon swap; added a `width <= 40rem` rule making the site-nav a single-row, horizontally-scrollable strip instead of wrapping to many lines. Turncount 22: fixed a real regression from turncount 21 -- the toggle button as a 3rd sibling flex item broke `.site-header .wrap`'s `justify-content: space-between` (tuned for exactly 2 children), landing orphaned on desktop and fully off-screen on mobile (neither `.site-nav` nor its `<ul>` could shrink below content size as flex items, since `min-width: 0`/overflow was on the wrong element). Fix, found and confirmed via real Playwright screenshots before and after: `.site-nav` is now itself `display: flex; min-width: 0;` containing the `<ul>` (now `flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0;`) and the button as its own children, restoring the outer header wrap to its original, correct 2-child layout.

assets/craft-progress.js.purpose: Shared vanilla-JS helper for the Craft course system (added turncount 14). Reads/writes localStorage key craft-progress as {courseId: {lessonId: true}}. Wires up quiz click handling (disable all options, mark correct/incorrect, reveal feedback, record completion on any answer), renders per-lesson progress checks on course-overview pages, and renders/unhides the course-level completion badge. No accounts, no server -- client-side only by design. Turncount 21: read in full during a dead-code audit -- every function confirmed reachable and called, no changes needed.

assets/theme.js.purpose: Added turncount 21 (QoL audit, explicit user ask for persistent themes). Reads/writes localStorage key 'theme' ('light'|'dark'). On DOMContentLoaded, applies the stored preference or falls back to prefers-color-scheme, sets data-theme on <html>, and wires the #theme-toggle button's click handler + aria-label/aria-pressed state. Paired with a tiny inline anti-flash script duplicated in every page's <head> (applies a stored theme before first paint, so there's no flash of the wrong theme) -- the duplication matches this repo's existing shared-nav-block precedent, since a build step to de-duplicate it doesn't exist and isn't warranted for one line.

RESEARCH FIRST: cross-checked multiple independent sources before touching content. Debunked the popular 'people remember 10%/20%/30%...90%' retention-ratio claim (often misattributed to Edgar Dale) as a fabricated statistic with no study behind it, confirmed via an ERIC-indexed journal article, a Wiley medical-education paper, and multiple learning-science analyses -- Dale's real Cone of Experience had no numbers on it and explicitly warned against reading it as a hierarchy. Confirmed what IS real and replicated instead: Mayer's Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning (coherence principle, segmenting principle), Sweller's Cognitive Load Theory (the worked-example effect), and Nielsen Norman Group's own usability-testing numbers (concise text alone: +58% usability; concise+scannable+objective together: +124%). Checked the actual page against the research rather than assuming it was an outlier: Typography's whyItMatters word count (368) was mid-pack among its 17 siblings, not uniquely long (spacing-layout 438, accessibility 402) -- the real finding was structural: the Typography Craft course was still on the pre-'v7' shallow 3-lesson format while its four siblings had been rebuilt to deep leveled courses, and the ExampleSide schema had no slot that could ever render an actual visual, only more text shaped like code.
